bookCredit: Number the Stars by Lois Lowry (1989) is quoted only in short lines.
title: Uncle Henrik’s Lunch

banner.alt: Early sun over a small harbor, a fishing boat at the dock, and a path coming out of dark woods

keepsake.name: scallop shell
keepsake.line: Only Imagination Trip travelers earn this one. It comes from the shore below the meadow, where you can look across to Sweden.

postcard.h: Bread, cheese, apple, and a packet
body: Annemarie is on the path with the basket when she hears a growl. What she carries matters more than she knows.
Build the basket as it reached Uncle Henrik.
postcard.word: A packet is a small wrapped bundle. This one sits at the bottom of the basket, under the napkin.

mission.h: Pack the basket for the boat
mission.p: Gather what reached Uncle Henrik and set it on the dock by the Ingeborg.

steps.build:
Open your menu (top button, right controller) and click Models. Build in this order:
  1. the Ingeborg and the nets by the dock
  2. the basket on the dock
  3. the apple and cheese in it
  4. the torn paper and handkerchief at the bottom
steps.say: Stand on the dock, like Annemarie. Practice these 2 sentences out loud:
steps.frame: “The soldier ___ the ___. That moment was ___ because ___.”
steps.extra: Put Sliced Bread back on the path: Mama’s loaf, broken in two for the dogs.
steps.fits: the boat, the nets and the basket

points: Your video is 30 seconds or less, shows the boat, nets and packed basket, and you say 2 sentences: one thing in the basket, what the soldier did with it, and why that was dangerous or lucky.

alt.p: By the end of Chapter 15, every part of the lunch has a place. Put each thing where it belongs.
alt.gameH: Tap a thing, then tap its place

spots.name: In the basket, in plain sight

items.why: The soldier breaks it in half and tosses the halves to the dogs.
He drops it in disgust. Annemarie picks it up again and runs.
He tosses it from hand to hand, then drops it back in the basket.
It lies in the bottom of the basket. Please, she thinks, don’t lift the napkin.
Under the napkin. He tears it open and finds only a folded white cloth.
Still there when she reaches the harbor, with Uncle Henrik kneeling by the nets.
He glances into the basket and sees the packet is there, even torn open.

alt.miss: Not there. Think about what the soldier did with it, and where it was when Annemarie reached the harbor.

write.q: Pick one thing in the basket. In 2 sentences, say what the soldier did with it and why that moment was dangerous or lucky, with one detail from Chapter 15.

scripts.brief: It is Grete. Annemarie is on the path with the basket when she hears a growl. In Chapter 15 she has only her voice, her face, and her mother’s advice. Build the harbor end of the chapter: the Ingeborg at the dock, the nets, and the basket as it reached Uncle Henrik. Then tell me which moment on the path was the closest call.
scripts.alt: No headset? Sit by the window with me and think about the lunch. By the end of the chapter, every part of it has a place: in plain sight, hidden at the bottom, gone to the dogs, or safe by the dock. Put each thing where it belongs.
scripts.saved: The basket reached the boat, and Uncle Henrik says everything is all right because of Annemarie. Here is your scallop shell from the shore below the meadow. Keep it, and remember that sometimes being brave looks like being a silly little girl.

labels.brief: Grete · the path to the harbor

testPara: The soldier tore open the packet and found the handkerchief. That moment was lucky because he laughed and flung it down, so Annemarie picked it up and brought it to Uncle Henrik.
